Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Fort Worth TX
558 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 

- A Heat Advisory is in effect for most of North and Central 
  Texas today. 

- The overall fire threat will be lower today due to increased
  cloud cover and lower wind speeds. However, continue to take
  caution to avoid sparking wildfires. Smoke from ongoing
  wildfires will continue to reduce visibility in some areas.
 
- Storm chances will be low today, mainly across western North
  Texas and Central Texas. There will be a potential for small
  hail and strong outflow winds. 

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today and tonight)
Issued at 228 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

The Southern Plains remains positioned on the eastern periphery 
of a mid-level area of high pressure, currently centered over the 
Four Corners region. This has allowed shortwaves to migrate 
southward into our region, bringing periods of showers and storms 
to the region. 

A weak boundary remains draped across the region early this 
morning with showers and storms ongoing eastern Central Texas. 
Given the 15-20 degree dew point depressions and modest 
instability, a few of these storms have become strong with gusty 
outflow winds and small hail. This activity is expected to 
continue moving south through the next few hours with mostly 
precipitation-free conditions closer to sunrise. 

A surface low will continue to deepen across Southeast Texas, 
influencing our region with north to northeasterly winds through 
much of the day. Even with the northerly wind component, 
temperatures this afternoon will manage to climb in the upper 90s 
to around 101 degrees. Hot temperatures combined with dew points 
in the mid to upper 60s will result in heat index values between 
100-109. The warmest "feel-like" temperatures will generally be
along and east of the I-35 corridor, where a Heat Advisory remains
in effect through this evening. 

Low rain chances will once again return this afternoon as weak 
forcing remains near the stalled boundary. Coverage should stay 
limited, but isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms may 
develop, especially across Central Texas and western portions of 
North Texas. The dry sub-cloud layer will limit rainfall totals, 
however, stronger cells will be capable of strong outflow winds 
and small hail. 

Tonight, expect precipitation chances to come to an end with
temperatures in the 70s across the region.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday through Wednesday)
Issued at 228 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Mid-level ridging highlighted in the short term discussion will 
continue to be the dominant feature through the rest of this 
forecast period. While the center of the high will remain well 
west of our region tomorrow, it's expected to start building back 
to the east this weekend. With increasing heights overhead, 
subsidence will help shunt precipitation chances away from our 
region. This translates into slightly warmer temperatures next 
week with widespread triple digit highs across much of North 
Texas. 

The position of the high will continue to influence our weather
next week as models now shift the center of the high east of our 
region, bringing deep southerly flow by the latter half of the
week. This could bring better moisture, helping temperatures drop
by a few degrees. Unfortunately, even with the potential for 
slightly cooler temperatures, heat index values are still going to
remain in the "it's too hot" category. 

Given the lack of wetting rainfall expected, the threat for new
fire starts will continue across the region. Vegetation remains
dry with afternoon relative humidity in the 20-30% range through
the middle of next week. Remember, you can help avoid wildfires! 
Do not burn if a burn ban is in effect and never throw cigarette 
butts out your window! 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 553 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

VFR conditions will persist across North and Central Texas TAF
sites today. Showers and storms are ongoing near KACT, however,
this activity continues to move south, away from the terminal.
Therefore, no mention of precipitation was added. 

The rest of today will be dry for North Texas, however, a few 
showers or storms may develop across Central Texas. Coverage is 
expected to remain low, therefore, confidence in precipitation 
impacting KACT remains too low to mention in TAF. This will 
continue to be assessed in the coming hours and amendments will be
made if probability of precipitation increases.

For North Texas, expect precipitation free conditions today. The
main weather headlines will be a gradual veering of winds through
the day, settling out of the southeast after 08z. Wind speeds 
will remain below 10 kts across the region. 

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...
Issued at 1200 PM CDT Sun Aug 23 2026

Spotter activation is not expected at this time.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Dallas-Ft. Worth   100  78  99  79 /  10  10   0   0 
Waco               101  75  98  75 /  10  10  10   0 
Paris               97  73  96  72 /  10   0   0   0 
Denton              99  74  99  74 /  10  10   0   0 
McKinney            99  74  98  74 /  10  10   0   0 
Dallas             101  78 100  79 /  10  10   0   0 
Terrell             99  73  99  73 /  10  10   0   0 
Corsicana          100  75  98  75 /  10  10   0   0 
Temple             102  75  99  74 /  20  20  10   0 
Mineral Wells      101  72 100  72 /  20  10   0   0 

&&

.FWD WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Heat Advisory until 8 PM CDT this evening for TXZ102>107-117>123-
131>135-144>148-157>162-174-175.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Hernandez
LONG TERM....Hernandez
AVIATION...Hernandez
